# Træk vejret helt ned i maven og bliv - måske - en bedre investor

**Feed**: millionaerklubben  
**Published**: 2026-09-09  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

This Danish episode of Millionærklubben (EuroInvestor) opens with the market: GameStop's better-than-expected results, which the guest strategist Michael Friis-Jørgensen dismisses, Meta's new Muse AI agent, Apple's product event, oil near $100 on Middle East escalation, and a weak Danish open led by pharma. The main segment asks whether leveraged, gamified trading is turning young men into gambling addicts. Guest psychologist Mads explains variable-ratio reward loops and argues that ordinary stock investing is fine, while leverage and prediction markets are dangerous. Mads also reviews his tech portfolio (+28% YTD, with a stop-loss rule now measured against sector peers) and says he still holds Ouster despite concern about its traffic-light business.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟡 OUST — Ouster | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Guest Mads still holds; his stop-loss has not triggered. The stock rose from about 21 to 37.49 since March. Its perception kit is broadly usable and the company is nearing break-even.

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion (Mads). Ouster's lidar, camera and sensor perception package fits agriculture, mining, warehouses, cars and robots, and its Gemini AI data platform could become the standard kit for physical AI. Sensor volumes are growing and the company is nearing break-even. His concern is management's focus on Blue City smart traffic lights, which he sees as a dead end. He trims only if the position exceeds 10% of the portfolio. Michael prefers exposure through a Chinese physical-AI ETF.

#### Sell Triggers

- stop-loss triggered by underperformance versus sector peers
- position exceeds 10% portfolio weight (trim)
- technology fails to be adopted or commercialised
- further strategic drift toward traffic-light end-market

> *"Nej, det har jeg ikke gjort. Okay, så du holder bare fast henover? Jeg er stadig i den her. Min stop-losses har ikke været aktiveret."*

---

### ⛔ GME — GameStop | **AVOID** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Michael flatly says it is not worth looking at despite the earnings beat. There is no structural case for physical used-games stores.

#### Reasoning

Opinion of Michael Friis-Jørgensen (the podcast's market strategist). The earnings beat is driven by investments such as the eBay stake and by collectibles, not by the core business. Physical game retail is in structural decline as games go digital. The stock's value comes from meme and brand status, not fundamentals, and he does not own it.

#### Sell Triggers

- core retail business returns to sustainable profitable growth
- successful eBay takeover transforms the business

> *"Hvad tænker du om situationen? Er det noget, der er værd at kigge på overhovedet? Nej."*

---

### 🟠 META — Meta | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

The Muse AI agent is a test case for consumer AI-agent adoption across 3bn users; Michael will follow whether it succeeds.

#### Reasoning

Michael thinks Meta is relatively strong on trust and has linked Muse to purchases, which protects its advertising model. With 3bn users it is the best gauge of whether consumers adopt AI agents. There is no buy call; he frames it as something to monitor for a consumer killer app. It is currently available only in the US.

#### Sell Triggers

- weak consumer adoption of Muse
- trust or privacy backlash over payment data

> *"Og det bliver jo skidespændende med meta, at prøve at måle, hvor det her bliver en succes, fordi det er jo 3 milliarder brugere"*
